_status: Which column of the firm's Docketwise export holds what, for tools/import_docketwise.py. EVERY column name below is an assumption: Docketwise's help pages say the Contacts tab and the Matters tab each have an export to a CSV file, but do not list the columns, so nothing here was seen in a real export. Each field lists the names to look for, in order; a heading matches when it is the same name ignoring capitals, spaces, underscores and hyphens. The firm edits this file after opening its own export: put the real heading first. Each section's _basis says, field by field, whether a name comes from a Docketwise report or API page (a name on a report or in the API, which is not proof of the CSV's heading) or is a plain guess. The importer's report says which headings it found and which it did not. TO CONFIRM WITH THE FIRM'S EXPORT.

_sources.says: Contacts tab and Matters tab each export to CSV (Export Contacts button, blue cloud icon). No column list, no mention of documents.
Third party. Matters: select all, More Actions, Export to CSV. Contacts: Export Contacts button. Gives no columns.
Contact report columns (a report's CSV, not necessarily the Contacts tab's): Full name, Daytime phone number, Mobile phone number, Email, Updated date, Matters, Assignees.
Matter report columns: Title, Client, Description, Updated, Priority date status, Assignees, Type, Status, Applicant, Preference category, Priority date.

API (JSON, not CSV): contact fields id, first_name, middle_name, last_name, email, type, lead, lead_phone, phone numbers (number, daytime). No language, consent or text-message opt-in field is documented.
API (JSON, not CSV): matter fields id, number, title, description, client_id, archived, status, type, receipt_number, priority_date.
Files sit in folders that can belong to a contact or a matter; files and folders can be bulk-downloaded (More Actions). The page does not say whether a zip is produced or how it is laid out.
